# Distribution plots with Seaborn

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

print("=== Creating Data ===\n")

np.random.seed(42)
data = pd.DataFrame({
    'Normal': np.random.normal(0, 1, 1000),
    'Skewed': np.random.exponential(1, 1000),
    'Bimodal': np.concatenate([
        np.random.normal(-2, 0.5, 500),
        np.random.normal(2, 0.5, 500)
    ])
})

print("Data created!")

print("\n=== Histogram ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 4))

plt.subplot(1, 3, 1)
sns.histplot(data['Normal'], bins=30, kde=True)
plt.title('Normal Distribution')

plt.subplot(1, 3, 2)
sns.histplot(data['Skewed'], bins=30, kde=True)
plt.title('Skewed Distribution')

plt.subplot(1, 3, 3)
sns.histplot(data['Bimodal'], bins=30, kde=True)
plt.title('Bimodal Distribution')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("\n=== KDE Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

sns.kdeplot(data['Normal'], label='Normal', shade=True)
sns.kdeplot(data['Skewed'], label='Skewed', shade=True)
sns.kdeplot(data['Bimodal'], label='Bimodal', shade=True)

plt.title('KDE Plots Comparison')
plt.xlabel('Value')
plt.ylabel('Density')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

print("\n=== Rug Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

sns.kdeplot(data['Normal'], shade=True)
sns.rugplot(data['Normal'], color='red', alpha=0.5)

plt.title('KDE with Rug Plot')
plt.xlabel('Value')
plt.ylabel('Density')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Ecdf Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

sns.ecdfplot(data['Normal'], label='Normal')
sns.ecdfplot(data['Skewed'], label='Skewed')
sns.ecdfplot(data['Bimodal'], label='Bimodal')

plt.title('ECDF Plots')
plt.xlabel('Value')
plt.ylabel('Cumulative Probability')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

print("\n=== Violin Plot ===\n")

# Create categorical data
data_cat = pd.DataFrame({
    'Group': np.repeat(['A', 'B', 'C'], 200),
    'Value': np.concatenate([
        np.random.normal(0, 1, 200),
        np.random.normal(2, 1.2, 200),
        np.random.normal(-1, 0.8, 200)
    ])
})

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

sns.violinplot(data=data_cat, x='Group', y='Value')
plt.title('Violin Plot by Group')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Box Plot with Swarm ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

sns.boxplot(data=data_cat, x='Group', y='Value', color='lightgray')
sns.swarmplot(data=data_cat, x='Group', y='Value', color='blue', alpha=0.5)

plt.title('Box Plot with Swarm Overlay')
plt.show()

phase1.explanation:
🐍 **Distribution plots show how data is distributed.**

**Plot types:**
| Plot | Best for |
|------|----------|
| Histogram | Overall shape |
| KDE | Smooth density |
| ECDF | Cumulative probability |
| Violin | Distribution by group |
| Box | Summary statistics |
| Swarm | Individual points |

**Distribution functions:**
```python
# Histogram with KDE
sns.histplot(data, kde=True)

# KDE only
sns.kdeplot(data, shade=True)

# ECDF
sns.ecdfplot(data)

# Rug plot (shows data points)
sns.rugplot(data)
```

**By group:**
```python
# Violin plot
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='group', y='value')

# Box plot
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='group', y='value')

# Swarm plot
sns.swarmplot(data=df, x='group', y='value')
```

**Python-chan says:**
"Distribution plots reveal the shape of your data. Always check distributions."

# Using too few bins in histogram

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)
data = np.random.normal(0, 1, 1000)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 4))

# Too few bins
plt.subplot(1, 3, 1)
sns.histplot(data, bins=2)
plt.title('2 Bins - Too Coarse')

# Good number of bins
plt.subplot(1, 3, 2)
sns.histplot(data, bins=30)
plt.title('30 Bins - Good')

# Too many bins
plt.subplot(1, 3, 3)
sns.histplot(data, bins=200)
plt.title('200 Bins - Too Detailed')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

phase2.explanation:
**Bin count changes the story!**

**What's wrong:**
1. Too few bins: oversimplifies
2. Too many bins: noise dominates
3. Both can mislead

**The fix:**
```python
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Method 1: Use automatic bin selection
sns.histplot(data, bins='auto')

# Method 2: Use Freedman-Diaconis rule
# bins = np.histogram(data, bins='fd')[1]

# Method 3: Try different values
for bins in [10, 20, 30, 50]:
    sns.histplot(data, bins=bins)
    plt.title(f'Bins: {bins}')
    plt.show()

# Method 4: Use KDE instead
sns.kdeplot(data)  # No bin selection needed

# Method 5: Use ECDF
sns.ecdfplot(data)  # No bin selection needed
```

**Python-chan says:**
"Bin count matters. Try different values or use KDE/ECDF instead."
